statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-40553 is a stack buffer overflow in ftype() in gawk's readdir extension (extension/readdir.c), which built 'dirname/d_name' into a PATH_MAX buffer with sprintf(). Debian's tracker names upstream commit cca03661 as the fix; with the follow-up bfa2e4b8 it bounds the copy with snprintf() and skips stat() when the name does not fit (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-40553, https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gawk.git/commit/?id=cca0366144336b49aaa7d5d949966ce8e2c70843, https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gawk.git/commit/?id=bfa2e4b890a44100a99d26b54af385479528b12e). DHI gawk for Alpine 3.23 packages gawk 5.3.2 and has three builds published by 2026-11-28: 5.3.2-r2, 5.3.2-r3 and 5.3.2-r4, each for x86_64 and aarch64. 5.3.2-r4 is the first build that carries a backport of both commits to 5.3.2. We disassembled usr/lib/gawk/readdir.so in all six builds: in 5.3.2-r4, ftype() compares the snprintf() result with 4095 and returns 'u' without calling stat() when it is larger; in 5.3.2-r2 and 5.3.2-r3 the call is Alpine's fortified sprintf() wrapper, which stops the process with a trap rather than writing past the buffer, so those builds still crash on an over-long path name and read as affected. 5.3.2-r3 was built without the backport.
